conviction_note: The Q3 numbers are new and not pre-released. There is no guidance and the financial targets were explicitly kept, so the move is sized on the new-numbers base. Attendo's own 11 observed report days have a median absolute move of 4.66% (the baseline's 2.33% sits on cadence-estimated dates), so abs_move is 6.0. The lean is only slightly up (p_up 55): peer Ambea's strong Q3 two days earlier, SEB still expecting Q3 margin gains in both segments after its downgrade, and the stock down 12% since late September while Ambea rose 7%, against a record Q3 2025 comparison base and a cut to SEB's Finland margin forecast. The bar is not sourced to a number (Modular Finance consensus exists but its estimate widget could not be read), so each finding is capped small. impact_sum (+0.2) and the scaled number (+0.6) agree in sign and are both small.

findings.finding: Closest peer Ambea reported a strong Q3 on 2026-11-04: adjusted EBITA SEK 668m (570), margin 15.0% (13.9), organic growth 5%. It cited higher occupancy and a 'kraftig resultatförbättring' at Vardaga (Swedish elderly care) and growth at Validia (Finland). That reads across to Attendo's Scandinavia and Finland occupancy story.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Attendo's reported-quarter surprises have moved it a lot: Q3 2025 'strongest quarter to date' +9.75%, Q4 2025 +12.0%. Q2 2026's 10.6% beat (EBITA 470 vs 425 Infront) moved it only +1.12%.
findings.original_quote: Vardaga redovisade ytterligare ett starkt kvartal med ökad beläggning och kraftig resultatförbättring. / Justerad EBITA ... uppgick till 668 (570) MSEK, motsvarande en marginal på 15,0 (13,9) procent. [Vardaga reported another strong quarter with higher occupancy and a sharp profit improvement. / Adjusted EBITA was SEK 668m (570), a margin of 15.0% (13.9).]
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: ATT rose 1.6% on 2026-11-04 (112.8 to 114.6) against +1.0% for OMXSPI, then gave back 0.8% on 11-05. Fully priced, it would have closed the gap since late September, when Ambea gained about 7% and ATT lost about 12%. It is a proxy, and Attendo is about 59% Finland where Ambea is mostly Sweden, so it is kept small.
findings.independence: SEB's 2026-10-08 note independently expects Q3 margin gains in both Attendo segments: https://www.placera.se/telegram/attendo-seb-sanker-attendo-till-behall--ser-mindre-an-10-procents-uppsida-20261008

findings.finding: SEB downgraded Attendo to hold on 2026-10-08 (target 132 from 134) and cut its Finland margin forecasts, while still expecting margin gains in both segments in Q3. The stock fell about 5% intraday and closed -2.7% on 4x normal volume. The bar has come down into the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of a pre-print downgrade found. The two prints after big drawdowns (Q3 2025 and Q4 2025) moved +9.75% and +12.0%.
findings.original_quote: Analyshuset räknar med fortsatta marginalförbättringar i båda segmenten under tredje kvartalet, drivet av högre beläggning och effektiviseringar. Därefter väntas tillväxten pressa marginalerna något. SEB sänker marginalprognoserna för Finland [The bank expects continued margin improvement in both segments in Q3, driven by higher occupancy and efficiencies; after that growth is expected to squeeze margins somewhat. SEB cuts its Finland margin forecasts]
findings.why_not_priced: The downgrade itself is priced (the same-day fall, and -12% from the 2026-09-22 high of 129.3 to 113.7). The finding is that the bar it left is lower. If the market thought the lowered bar was still too high, ATT would not have rebounded with Ambea on 11-04. Kept small because the number is unsourced.

findings.finding: Finland's private social-services collective agreement (Hali and the unions, 27 Feb 2026) carries 6.1% pay rises (snippet only). That is a labour-cost headwind on Attendo Finland (about 59% of sales), where welfare-region price indexation lags. It is plausibly behind SEB's Finland margin cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 Finland lease-adjusted EBITA margin rose to 8.4% (6.7) despite the agreement, so this cost has not shown up in prints so far.

findings.finding: The comparison base is the record quarter. Q3 2025 lease-adjusted EBITA was SEK 482m (10.1% margin) at 87% occupancy, against Q2 2025's 205m at 85%. Occupancy was 88% at end-Q2 2026, so the yoy occupancy tailwind narrows from +3pp to about +1pp and headline EBITA growth slows sharply from +57%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 on this base: +9.75%. Q2 2026, where headline growth was flattering: only +1.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts model the base, so this is mostly priced. It is filed because a slower headline growth rate is what a headline-driven open reads first. An inference from primary documents, kept small.
